answers.explanation: Each system call has a number, and the table maps numbers to implementations.
The system-call interface sits right at the user/kernel boundary.
That's how read() can hand back a byte count or -1.
The caller only needs to obey the API and know what the OS will do.
The library functions set up and make the actual system calls.
printf() is a library call; write() is the system call underneath.
The trap switches to kernel mode, then the interface consults the table.
Library calls run in user mode; some of them make system calls.
